description: We are a team of students participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Together, we are developing a 2D lunar survival simulation that combines game development, science, and space exploration. We are designing the habitat, programming interactive tasks and minigames, and researching real space missions to create an engaging educational experience. Our goal is to inspire younger audiences to explore science, technology, and space.
summary:
Developed by team WAAVES using Godot, VS Code, and Claude; Habitat Zero is a junior astronaut mission trainer designed to make space exploration interactive and educational for younger audiences.

The game addresses the challenge of making lunar science engaging by putting players in the boots of an astronaut tasked with surviving five days on the Moon. Players must carefully balance keeping their habitat stable against random emergency events while conducting research to earn points.

This project is important because it simulates realistic lunar environments, sparks children's interest in astronomy, and transforms abstract space concepts into hands-on experiences. By incorporating NASA data and planning a public release, Habitat Zero inspires the next generation of space explorers to learn what it truly takes to live and work on other worlds.
details: Our project is a 2D educational simulation designed to teach younger players what it takes to live and work on the Moon. Players take on the role of an astronaut living in a lunar habitat, where they must survive a five-day mission by maintaining equipment, conducting scientific research, and responding to unexpected emergencies. Each day, players have limited time to complete tasks, so they must decide whether to prioritize research or the safety of their habitat. Events such as equipment failures, moon dust buildup, micrometeoroid impacts, and solar flares challenge players to think critically and solve problems. Our goal is to make learning about space exploration more interactive and accessible while sparking curiosity about astronomy, science, and engineering. We wanted to go beyond a typical space game by including realistic challenges astronauts could face during a lunar mission and showing how everyday maintenance and scientific experiments are essential for survival. We developed the game using the Godot game engine, GDScript, Visual Studio Code, and Claude for AI assistance. Throughout development, our team considered how to make the experience both educational and enjoyable, balancing realistic space related challenges with gameplay that younger audiences could understand. We also explored how NASA research and real lunar mission data could help make the game's scenarios more accurate and meaningful. Through this project, we hope to give players a better appreciation of the challenges of living beyond Earth and inspire the next generation of space explorers.
